subject: DataForge discovery — sample queries, redaction checklist, and model recs
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@dataforge.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@dataforge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-15T15:24:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + ask: sample queries & redaction guidance

Hi Evan / Priya — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap of the things we discussed and a few concrete asks to move the evaluation forward: 

1) Primary objective: reduce time-to-insight on customer support tickets (priority triage + canned summary + suggested next action).
2) Data shape: email-like tickets (up to ~2,500 tokens), mix of short and long histories, some HTML, occasional log snippets.
3) Security: must never return raw credit card numbers or personal identifiers in model output; audit logs required.

Next steps we need from you so we can prepare a tailored eval pack: 
- A sampling (500–1,000 rows) of user queries and associated expected outputs or labels. CSV is perfect. Redact or mark PII where needed — see the attached example file for format.
- A short list of edge cases you care about (examples: multi-turn threading, code snippets, attachments referenced inline, mixed languages).
- Any hard guardrails (blacklisted terms, legal phrases) we should enforce in the eval.

From our side, we will: 
- Propose 2 model profiles (cost-optimized and quality-optimized) with benchmark links and prompts.
- Produce a minimal prompt set + redaction checklist you can apply before upload.

I’ve attached a tiny sample CSV and a redaction examples file to illustrate the format. Can you confirm if 500 rows is feasible by Monday?

Cheers,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

---
Attachment stubs: dataforge_sample_queries.csv (csv, 23KB), pii_examples_for-redaction.txt (txt, 6KB)

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@dataforge.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Liu <evan.liu@dataforge.ai>
Date: 2028-02-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask: sample queries & redaction guidance

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the clear list. We can do 600 rows by Monday. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The dataset will include HTML snippets and occasional base64 inline attachments (we can provide a flag column to indicate those).
- For PII, we can either fully redact (replace with [REDACTED]) or provide annotated columns indicating start/end spans. Which do you prefer for model evaluation?
- Edge cases: 1) tickets with code blocks, 2) tickets where the user pastes a stack trace and then asks a follow-up, 3) non-English (primarily Spanish) short tickets.

Also, curious what you had in mind for the two model profiles and rough latency expectations — we need to align on SLOs before the PoC.

Thanks,
Priya
Head of Product, DataForge AI
priya.shah@dataforge.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-16T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick recap + ask: sample queries & redaction guidance — plan to respond

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Priya’s clarifications. Proposed internal plan: 

- Redaction approach: request annotated spans from DataForge if possible. If not, accept full redact with [REDACTED] and tag the column type (email, phone, card). Annotated spans give us better eval signal but redacted tokens are fine for initial qual.
- Model profiles to recommend in the reply: 
  * Quality-first: rw-align-13b (float16) — target latency ~90–150ms/token on dedicated p4d; expected highest ROUGE/accuracy on abstractive summaries.
  * Cost-balanced: rw-instruct-7b-4bit — good for throughput (lower token cost) with a small hit to abstractive quality but still strong on classification/triage tasks.

- Benchmarks to include in our external reply: link to the public Redwood chat-model latency/cost page, and an internal eval doc with sample expected metrics (ROUGE, F1 for triage labels, hallucination checks).

Action items for us: I’ll draft an external reply with the ask for annotated spans and an outline of the eval pack we’ll run. Ben — can you attach the public benchmark link and the minimal prompt templates (1–2 exemplars for summary + triage) to that reply?

Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@dataforge.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@dataforge.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-17T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask: sample queries & redaction guidance — model suggestions + uploads

Hi Priya / Evan — great to hear 600 rows is possible. A few concrete items from Redwood to get you unstuck: 

1) Redaction recommendation: if you can provide annotated spans (start/end indices + label) that’s ideal for our eval pipeline. If annotation isn’t feasible, send a redacted CSV and a small sample of non-redacted rows in a secure channel (we can treat them as private eval-only samples).

2) Model profiles (two options we suggest for your PoC):
   - Quality-first: rw-align-13b (fp16) — strong abstractive summarization, recommended when summaries must be fluent and concise. We’ll run hallucination checks and ROUGE/LQA.
   - Cost-balanced: rw-instruct-7b-4bit — lower inference cost, good throughput with modest quality tradeoffs; recommended for routing/triage + quick suggested actions.

3) SLO / latency guidance: for interactive triage (sub-200ms/token median) we recommend a dedicated instance; for batch nightly processing, the 7b option provides better unit economics.

4) Prompt examples attached (two templates): short summary prompt + triage classifier few-shot examples. We’ll also include a tiny benchmark link so you can compare latency & cost estimates side-by-side.

Attachments in this thread: redwood_summary_and_triage_prompts.txt (plain text), redwood_latency_benchmarks.pdf (public summary).

Please upload the CSV to the secure S3 link we’ll send via separate email (we don’t accept PII over regular email). If you want, we can run a one-day model calibration after upload and return a short eval report.

Next step: can you confirm whether the annotated spans are feasible or if we should expect fully redacted rows? If annotated spans are feasible, we’ll share the exact CSV schema.

Thanks — looking forward to the PoC.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
